hebb_eps_exponent.cite: exponent of eps ~ alpha^(-1/2) for online Hebb learning: Biehl & Riegler, 'On-line learning with a perceptron', Europhys. Lett. 28, 525 (1994); read: the authors' preprint (biehl.online-perceptron.ps.gz, www.cs.rug.nl/~biehl/Publications/prepbefore.html, dated Jul 1994, marked 'submitted to Europhysics Letters'; journal version not checked), abstract ('(N/P)^(1/2) behavior of the so-called Hebbian learning') and Eq. (7) (citing Vallet, Europhys. Lett. 9, 315 (1989), not fetched); also Vicente, Kinouchi & Caticha, 'Statistical mechanics of online learning of drifting concepts: a variational approach', Machine Learning 32, 179 (1998), arXiv:cond-mat/9801297v1 (PDF read), Tables I-II, column D = 0, chi = 0 ('0.40 alpha^-1/2', annealed Hebb). Convention (BR Eqs. (1)-(6)): |B| = 1, inputs with i.i.d. zero-mean unit-variance components, J <- J + (1/N) f b xi, alpha = P/N, eps = arccos(rho)/pi the probability of disagreeing with the teacher; replicant's eta = 1 and noise = 0 are BR's setting. tol 1e-3: replicant's measured log-slope differs from 1/2 by 3.4e-6 at alpha = 1e4
hebb_eps_exponent.independent_route: replicant's ODE (online/odes.py: the rates dR/dalpha, dQ/dalpha from the closed-form Gaussian averages of online/fields.py, integrated in (theta, ln Q) by Dormand-Prince 5(4), rtol 1e-9 (1e-8 relative on the constants), from (R0, Q0) = (0, 1)) to alpha = 1e4: the exponent is the log-slope of eps between 5e3 and 1e4, the constant alpha^p eps at 1e4 with p derived (online/odes.py EXPONENT); the averages are checked against an independent polar quadrature (tests/test_online_perceptron.py) and the ODE against finite-N simulation over named seeds (online/simulate.py, tests/test_online_noise_sim.py)

(1)-(6)): |B| = 1, inputs with i.i.d. zero-mean unit-variance components, J <- J + (1/N) f b xi, alpha = P/N, eps = arccos(rho)/pi the probability of disagreeing with the teacher; replicant's eta = 1 and noise = 0 are BR's setting. tol 1e-5: the ODE at alpha = 1e4 is 9.4e-7 below the limit (its O(1/alpha) correction); the Hebb closed form at alpha = 1e12 agrees to 1e-12
hebb_eps_constant.independent_route: replicant's ODE (online/odes.py: the rates dR/dalpha, dQ/dalpha from the closed-form Gaussian averages of online/fields.py, integrated in (theta, ln Q) by Dormand-Prince 5(4), rtol 1e-9 (1e-8 relative on the constants), from (R0, Q0) = (0, 1)) to alpha = 1e4: the exponent is the log-slope of eps between 5e3 and 1e4, the constant alpha^p eps at 1e4 with p derived (online/odes.py EXPONENT); the averages are checked against an independent polar quadrature (tests/test_online_perceptron.py) and the ODE against finite-N simulation over named seeds (online/simulate.py, tests/test_online_noise_sim.py); and the closed form R = eta a alpha, Q - R^2 = Q0 + eta^2 alpha, a = sqrt(2/pi) (derived in online/odes.py hebb_closed_form; the ODE matches it to 1e-8)

optimal_eps_constant.cite: asymptotic constant of eps ~ C/alpha for the optimal online rule (noiseless, rho known): Vicente, Kinouchi & Caticha, 'Statistical mechanics of online learning of drifting concepts: a variational approach', Machine Learning 32, 179 (1998), arXiv:cond-mat/9801297v1 (PDF read), Tables I and II, column e_G(D = 0, chi = 0): '0.88 alpha^-1' (Optimal); Biehl & Riegler, 'On-line learning with a perceptron', Europhys. Both are secondary for Kinouchi & Caticha 1992 (not fetched). Two digits printed: tol 0.005 covers the rounding. replicant: 0.88318 from the ODE at alpha = 1e4; the rho -> 1 limit 2/I(0) = 0.883400 (online/optimal.py, mpmath)
optimal_eps_constant.independent_route: replicant's ODE (online/odes.py: the rates dR/dalpha, dQ/dalpha from the closed-form Gaussian averages of online/fields.py, integrated in (theta, ln Q) by Dormand-Prince 5(4), rtol 1e-9 (1e-8 relative on the constants), from (R0, Q0) = (0, 1)) to alpha = 1e4: the exponent is the log-slope of eps between 5e3 and 1e4, the constant alpha^p eps at 1e4 with p derived (online/odes.py EXPONENT); the averages are checked against an independent polar quadrature (tests/test_online_perceptron.py) and the ODE against finite-N simulation over named seeds (online/simulate.py, tests/test_online_noise_sim.py); and the mpmath integral 2/I(0), I = int Dt e^{-t^2/2}/H(t), of the rho -> 1 limit of the optimal flow (derived in online/optimal.py; agreement 2e-3 at alpha = 1e4 tested)

no_learning_boundary_l0p3.cite: noise estimate Lam below which the optimal rule (built on Lam) does not learn at true output-noise level lam = 0.3: Lam = 2 lam - 1/2 (Copelli, Eichhorn, Kinouchi, Biehl, Simonetti, Riegler & Caticha, 'Noise robustness in multilayer neural networks', Europhys. Lett. 37, 427 (1997), DOI 10.1209/epl/i1997-00167-2; read: the preprint WUE-ITP-96-022 (www.cs.rug.nl/~biehl/Publications/WUE/WUE-ITP-96-022.ps.gz, Oct 1996; journal version not checked), p. 5: 'imperfect learning will occur unless Lambda_o is less than 2 lambda_o - 1/2 where d rho/d alpha|rho=0 becomes negative'; the dashed line of Fig. 1a, which a pixel reading confirms: 0.100, 0.200, 0.300 at lam = 0.3, 0.35, 0.4). Output noise: P(label inverted) = lam (their Eq. (7)); their result holds for every K of the tree committee and parity machines, K = 1 being the perceptron (p. 5). Convention (BR Eqs. (1)-(6)): |B| = 1, inputs with i.i.d. zero-mean unit-variance components, J <- J + (1/N) f b xi, alpha = P/N, eps = arccos(rho)/pi the probability of disagreeing with the teacher; replicant's eta = 1 and noise = 0 are BR's setting. The value is the printed formula evaluated. tol 1e-6: replicant's bisection resolves 1e-13, its rho = 1e-6 evaluation point shifts the root by O(rho)
no_learning_boundary_l0p3.independent_route: replicant: bisection in Lam on the sign of drho/dalpha of the ODE flow at rho = 1e-6 (online/optimal.py noise_boundaries, closed-form averages of fields.py), not the formula; the trajectory below the line decays to rho = 0 (tests/test_online_noise_sim.py)
